title: Exactness of analytic pullback for algebraic module sheaves
statement: Let $X$ be a separated finite-type smooth scheme over $\mathbf C$ with analytification $\pi:M\to X$ as in [lem-sfb-smooth-analytification-cotangent]. For every short exact sequence of $\mathcal O_X$-module sheaves $0\to F'\to F\to F''\to0$, the sequence of analytic module sheaves $0\to F'^{\mathrm{an}}\to F^{\mathrm{an}}\to F''^{\mathrm{an}}\to0$ is exact. No finite-generation hypothesis on the modules is required.

source.place: WANTED: Serre, Géométrie algébrique et géométrie analytique, §9 Prop.10 and §6 Prop.3 corollary, printed pp.16--18; exactness follows from flatness of analytic local rings.

proof.text: Fix $a\in M$ and put $x=\pi(a)$, $A=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ and $B=\mathcal O_{M,a}$. The local comparison lemma gives Noetherian local rings $A,B$ and the canonical isomorphism $\widehat A\simeq\widehat B$. Its compatibility with the two completion maps makes this an $A$-algebra isomorphism for the actual map $A\to B$; it is not merely an abstract isomorphism of complete rings.

source.place: (3), supporting GAGA prerequisite chain; agent proof of analytic exactness, with the absent Serre source recorded WANTED

proof.text: Apply faithful flatness of Noetherian local completion first to $A$ and then to $B$. Thus $\widehat A$ is flat over $A$, while $B\to\widehat B$ is faithfully flat. The preceding $A$-algebra isomorphism makes $\widehat B$ flat over $A$. Apply faithfully flat descent of module flatness to $A\to B\to C=\widehat B$ and the $B$-module $N=B$: the map $C\otimes_BB\to C$, $c\otimes b\mapsto cb$, is an $A$-linear isomorphism with inverse $c\mapsto c\otimes1$. The descent equivalence therefore says that $B$ is flat over $A$.

Forget the module structures in the given short exact sequence. The sectionwise kernel and sheafified-cokernel formulas for module sheaves are the same as for the underlying abelian sheaves: the module action on a kernel is its restricted action, and on a cokernel is the quotient action followed by sheafification. Thus forgetting preserves and reflects exactness. The short-exact stalk criterion gives $0\to F'_x\to F_x\to F''_x\to0$ for every $x\in X$. The same criterion on $M$ will detect exactness of the analytic sequence.

source.place: Tag 01AG (lemma-abelian); sheaves.tex Section 007S, exactness at points

proof.text: View the analytification morphism of ringed spaces as the corresponding morphism of ringed sheaf topoi, and take the point defined by $a\in M$. Its composite point evaluates germs at $x=\pi(a)$: a neighbourhood $V$ of $x$ pulls back to the neighbourhood $\pi^{-1}V$ of $a$. The ringed-topos pullback-stalk comparison applies to the defining tensor pullback and yields $(F^{\mathrm{an}})_a\cong F_x\otimes_AB$, and likewise for $F'$ and $F''$. Naturality identifies both analytic stalk maps with the original stalk maps tensored with $1_B$. In particular these identifications compare the actual sequence maps.

source.place: Tag 05V5 (lemma-pullback-stalk), applied to the morphism of topological sheaf topoi of π; compare sheaves.tex Tag 0098 (lemma-stalk-pullback-modules)

proof.text: Tensor the short exact stalk sequence with $B$ over $A$. Right exactness of tensor gives exactness at $F_x\otimes_AB$ and surjectivity onto $F''_x\otimes_AB$. Flatness of $B$ gives injectivity of $F'_x\otimes_AB\to F_x\otimes_AB$ by the defining injectivity criterion. Hence the analytic sequence is short exact at every $a\in M$, and the stalk criterion of step 3 gives the claimed short exact sequence of analytic module sheaves. The argument applies to arbitrary stalk modules: no coherence, quasi-coherence or finite-generation assumption occurs.
